rationale: C11 plausibly supplied a material structural template: the President assigns a trusted personal representative a significant fact-finding task, directs him to obtain the views of affected or knowledgeable groups, and explains that the resulting understanding will guide future policy. The child adapts that machinery specifically to consultation with major tribal groups. C22 has a similar commissioned inquiry and recommendation structure, while C16 shares some assignment and purpose language but lacks the child’s consultation-to-policy sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am asking you, as my personal representative, to go into the home territory of the Indians ... and meet with each of the major tribal groups
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have decided to appoint you as Special Assistant to the President to assist in this task.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters personally designate the recipient to undertake a presidential fact-finding assignment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it is essential for us to learn firsthand their thoughts, needs, and aspirations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I shall also look to you to obtain the views of experts and interested groups outside the Government on particular aspects of the problem.
shared_material.explanation: Both assignments center on gathering views directly from relevant groups beyond ordinary internal agency channels.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Only with such knowledge can we move forward ... in shaping policies and programs
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The first phase of our work is to determine the nature, dimensions, and significance of this problem. In the light of this understanding, we must develop the broad lines of policy
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive operative logic is the same: collect information and viewpoints first, then use that understanding to formulate policy.
